meaning: FELV is an extra-low-voltage system that does not meet all of the protective requirements needed to qualify as SELV or PELV.
studyNote: The voltage may be extra-low, but that alone does not give FELV the same protective status as SELV or PELV; the missing protective measures must be accounted for.
distinction: SELV and PELV are defined protective systems; FELV is used where the extra-low voltage is functional but all SELV/PELV protective provisions are not present.

meaning: Leakage current is current flowing in an unintended conductive path during normal operating conditions.
studyNote: It can contribute to protective-conductor current and residual current even when no insulation fault is present.
distinction: Leakage current occurs under normal operation; fault current results from a fault.

meaning: PELV is an extra-low-voltage system that meets the protective requirements of SELV except that it is not electrically separated from Earth.
studyNote: It retains the extra-low-voltage protective concept while allowing an intentional connection to Earth where the system design permits it.
distinction: SELV is separated from Earth; PELV may be connected to Earth.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide treats SELV and PELV together as recognized shock-protection methods and later gives verification requirements for SELV/PELV circuit separation.

meaning: A reduced low-voltage system, in the supplied historical definition, is limited to 110 V nominal line-to-line and 63.5 V nominal line-to-Earth.
studyNote: It is a specific reduced-voltage arrangement and should not be assumed to be the same thing as SELV or PELV.
distinction: The stated voltage limits are from the supplied 2015 definition; do not generalize them into a current local requirement without checking the applicable standard and jurisdiction.

meaning: SELV is an extra-low-voltage system electrically separated from Earth and from other systems so that a single fault cannot create the defined electric-shock risk.
studyNote: Its protection depends on both the low voltage and the required electrical separation; merely measuring a low voltage does not make a circuit SELV.
distinction: PELV otherwise meets SELV requirements but is not electrically separated from Earth.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide lists SELV/PELV as recognized shock-protection methods and includes separation checks for SELV and PELV circuits during verification.

meaning: Simple separation is separation between circuits, or between a circuit and Earth, using basic insulation only.
studyNote: It provides a defined separation function but not the additional insulation or protective screening that makes separation 'protective'.
distinction: Protective separation uses double insulation, reinforced insulation, or basic insulation plus protective screening.

meaning: Nominal voltage is the voltage value used to designate an installation or part of it. The supplied historical definition also divides nominal voltage into extra-low, low and high ranges.
studyNote: Nominal voltage is a classification or designation value, not a guarantee that every measured instantaneous voltage will exactly equal that number.
distinction: The quoted voltage bands are those of the supplied 2015 BS 7671 definition; always check the current applicable standard and local requirements before using them for compliance decisions.
